name: 3Blue1Brown (Grant Sanderson)
shortDescription: Mathematics rebuilt visually, so the ideas arrive as pictures with reasons attached rather than as procedures to memorise.

name: Abbie Emmons
shortDescription: A novelist teaching fiction craft through short technique videos and long write-along sessions, wrapped in a substantial paid ecosystem.

name: Alan Becker Tutorials
shortDescription: A closed archive whose main asset is a complete, well-made series on the twelve principles of animation.

name: Alexander Lyon Communication Coach
shortDescription: A tenured communication professor teaching workplace communication — empathy, listening, teamwork and leadership — in a plain lecture style.

name: Andrew Huang
shortDescription: A working multi-genre musician whose channel mixes real production technique with a great deal of entertainment and experiment.

name: Vinh Giang
shortDescription: An Australian communication coach who teaches vocal delivery, body language and conversational technique, mostly through very short clips with a smaller long-form catalogue behind them.

name: Benjamin Keep
shortDescription: A cognitive scientist who spends much of his time explaining why popular learning advice — including the advice everyone repeats — does not survive the research.

name: Better Ideas (Joey Schweitzer)
shortDescription: Self-improvement essays that keep circling back to why the previous advice failed, including his own.

name: Buzzsprout
shortDescription: A podcast-hosting company's channel: practical launch-and-growth guidance plus long interviews with people who make podcasts well.

name: ByteByteGo
shortDescription: Animated system-design explainers from the authors of the System Design Interview books — clear, consistent, and shaped by the interview format.

name: Charisma on Command
shortDescription: Breaks down charisma and social confidence by analysing clips of well-known people frame by frame, then naming the specific behaviour that produced the effect.

name: Coffeezilla
shortDescription: Investigations into scams and self-styled gurus, showing the paper trail rather than asserting that something smells wrong.

name: Conor Neill
shortDescription: A business-school lecturer in Spain with a long back catalogue on speaking and persuasion, whose newer output has moved toward leadership.

name: ContraPoints
shortDescription: A former philosophy academic making a handful of very long, heavily staged essays on how people come to believe and want things.

name: Corey Schafer
shortDescription: Long, unhurried Python tutorials that explain the language properly rather than racing to a finished app — the closest thing here to a textbook on video.

name: Database Star (Ben Brumm)
shortDescription: Practical SQL for people who already write it — performance rules, real query post-mortems, and the business calculations nobody teaches.

name: Andy Stapleton
shortDescription: Academic-career and research-workflow advice from a former academic, now heavily focused on AI tools — including their failure modes.

name: Dreaming Spanish
shortDescription: Spanish taught entirely in Spanish, pitched so that a total beginner can follow from context — the comprehensible-input method done at scale.
languageNote: The uploads are in Spanish, not English — deliberately. This is a comprehensible-input channel, where hearing the target language you can almost follow IS the teaching method, so an English version of these videos would not be the same resource. Included under the named exemption in project rule 5. No prior Spanish is assumed: the beginner videos are built to be understood from context, gesture and drawing alone.

name: Dr. Tracey Marks
shortDescription: A board-certified psychiatrist translating neuroscience into short, plain explanations — heavily short-form, so treat it as reference rather than curriculum.

name: Duarte, Inc.
shortDescription: The channel of a presentation consultancy that has been building corporate talks since 1988, aimed squarely at people who present to executives.

name: Exam Study Expert (William Wadsworth)
shortDescription: Exam technique built on learning science rather than study aesthetics — the rare channel here that treats sitting an exam as its own distinct skill.

name: Film Riot
shortDescription: A long-running, deliberately energetic filmmaking how-to show, strongest on practical effects and on getting a scene shot at all.

name: Folding Ideas (Dan Olson)
shortDescription: Long documentary essays that reconstruct how a false belief or a financial scheme was actually built, rather than just mocking the people inside it.

name: Gareth David Studio
shortDescription: A working creative director teaching graphic design as a commercial discipline with constraints, not as self-expression.

name: Game Maker's Toolkit (Mark Brown)
shortDescription: Design analysis of released games — why a mechanic works, what difficulty is for — from someone who also runs one of the largest game jams and ships his own work.

name: HealthyGamerGG (Dr. Alok Kanojia)
shortDescription: A psychiatrist explaining the mechanisms under motivation, avoidance and burnout — and frequently arguing that the popular self-improvement framing has them backwards.

name: Tim Hickson (Hello Future Me)
shortDescription: A New Zealand author making long video essays on worldbuilding and narrative craft, mixed with a great deal of franchise criticism.

name: Hussein Nasser
shortDescription: Backend internals explained one layer down — how a database or a protocol actually behaves, not how to call it.

name: How Communication Works
shortDescription: A college professor and research scientist teaching listening, repair and conversation technique, with an explicit claim to an evidence base.

name: How to ADHD (Jessica McCabe)
shortDescription: Strategies for getting started on things, built by someone with ADHD and useful well beyond it — including the best available name for task paralysis.

name: In Depth Cine
shortDescription: Technical cinematography explained for people about to walk onto a set for the first time, with the trade-offs stated rather than hidden.

name: In The Mix (Michael Wynne)
shortDescription: A Scottish audio engineer teaching mixing and mastering in short, concrete lessons — while also selling his own plugins in a growing share of them.

name: Jefferson Fisher
shortDescription: A practising trial lawyer who teaches people to argue less and stay in control of tense conversations, in both short clips and long podcast-style episodes.

name: JustinGuitar (Justin Sandercoe)
shortDescription: The long-standing free guitar curriculum — a structured beginner-to-advanced course that happens to live on YouTube and a website.

name: Justin Sung
shortDescription: A former doctor turned learning coach teaching a research-flavoured system for reading, note-taking and retention — inside a large paid-coaching business.

name: Kevin Powell
shortDescription: A CSS specialist — one language, taught for years, by someone who thinks it is genuinely interesting rather than an obstacle.

name: Lessons from the Screenplay
shortDescription: A closed archive of sixty-eight screenplay analyses, reading scripts against the finished films to show how the structure was built.

name: Linking Your Thinking (Nick Milo)
shortDescription: Personal knowledge management in Obsidian — strong on what notes are for, increasingly preoccupied with AI tooling.

name: Luca Lampariello
shortDescription: Twenty years of language learning distilled into method rather than polyglot spectacle, taught in English about learning any language.

name: Manager Tools
shortDescription: Two thousand-plus episodes of unglamorous, highly specific management guidance, mostly half-hour audio with a slide behind it.

name: Marco Bucci
shortDescription: A professional concept artist teaching colour, light and material — the painting half of the craft that figure-drawing channels leave out.

name: Eddie Woo
shortDescription: A working high-school maths teacher publishing his actual lessons — five thousand of them — filmed in the classroom.

name: Modern Software Engineering (Dave Farley)
shortDescription: Argued positions on how software should be built and tested, from a practitioner who is happy to tell you the common practice is wrong.

name: münecat
shortDescription: Feature-length debunks of the self-improvement industry itself — body-language experts, motivational gurus, multi-level marketing — from an openly left-wing critic.

name: NeetCode
shortDescription: Worked algorithm-problem solutions explained as reasoning rather than as answers — plus, increasingly, industry commentary that is not that.

name: Chris Voss & The Black Swan Group
shortDescription: The channel of Chris Voss and the Black Swan Group, teaching a negotiation method built on tactical empathy and calibrated questions.

name: Nelson Dellis
shortDescription: A six-time US memory champion teaching the actual competitive techniques, and unusually clear that they are trainable rather than innate.

name: New York Vocal Coaching (Justin Stoney)
shortDescription: A voice teacher answering singers' technical questions in a long-running numbered episode series, plus vocal analyses of well-known performers.

name: Nigel Danson
shortDescription: Landscape photography with an unusual emphasis on composition and on small changes that measurably improve an image.

name: Nielsen Norman Group
shortDescription: The research consultancy that largely defined usability as a discipline, publishing short evidence-based explainers plus a longer interview series.

name: The Oxford Union
shortDescription: Full formal debates from a two-hundred-year-old debating society, published alongside the individual speeches that make them up.

name: Patrick Teahan
shortDescription: A therapist using role-play to show what dysfunctional family dynamics actually sound like — and, unusually, what good therapy looks like.

name: Sam Laura Brown
shortDescription: A long-running podcast on perfectionism specifically, strongest on why standard productivity advice fails perfectionists — now aimed largely at business owners.

name: Philipp Lackner
shortDescription: Android and Kotlin taught with the reasoning attached — explicitly aimed at developers who want to know why, not just make it compile.

name: Pianote
shortDescription: A subscription piano school's channel — competent adult-beginner teaching, wrapped tightly around a free-trial pitch.

name: PremiumBeat by Shutterstock
shortDescription: A stock-music company's back catalogue of After Effects and post-production tutorials, dormant since 2025 but still a solid technique library.

name: Proko (Stan Prokopenko)
shortDescription: Structured figure-drawing and anatomy instruction from an artist-teacher, in long lessons that build in a deliberate order.

name: Radical Candor
shortDescription: The channel built around Kim Scott's feedback framework — caring personally while challenging directly — mostly as long interviews with people who have to do it.

name: Rationality Rules (Stephen Woodford)
shortDescription: Argument analysis applied to real debates, with genuinely useful technique buried under aggressively adversarial framing.

name: Gregory B. Sadler (ReasonIO)
shortDescription: A finished thirty-three-video lecture series on logical fallacies by a philosophy PhD, dormant since 2015 and none the worse for it.

name: Refold
shortDescription: A single opinionated immersion method for learning any language, taught in English, with unusually concrete flashcard technique attached.

name: Megan Devine
shortDescription: A therapist and author on grief who rejects the stages-and-recovery framing outright, and talks about the parts nobody warns you about.

name: Rex Krueger
shortDescription: Hand-tool woodworking for people without a workshop or a budget, built around getting you to make something rather than buy something.

name: Satori Graphics
shortDescription: A large graphic-design catalogue covering theory as well as tools, with a recent and heavy pivot toward AI content.

name: Shaelin Bishop (ShaelinWrites)
shortDescription: A literary fiction writer and MFA student talking craft at length, with no short-form content at all and almost nothing for sale.

name: Skillopedia
shortDescription: Plain, beginner-level soft-skills lessons in English, dormant since 2024 — useful mainly as a starting point for people the rest of this list would overwhelm.

name: StatQuest with Josh Starmer
shortDescription: Statistics and machine learning decomposed into small steps and worked through in full — including the matrix algebra most explanations skip.

name: StoryCorps
shortDescription: Ordinary people interviewing each other, published as short animated pieces — plus the rare thing of an actual masterclass in how to ask.

name: StudioBinder
shortDescription: Well-produced video essays on how specific directors and films work, made by a production-management software company.

name: Stumpy Nubs (James Hamilton)
shortDescription: Practical shop technique and blunt tool assessments, focused on the problems that ruin work rather than on showpiece projects.

name: TechWorld with Nana
shortDescription: Long, structured DevOps and cloud tutorials — full crash courses rather than tips, from a practitioner with vendor credentials.

name: The Closer Look
shortDescription: Long, argumentative essays on narrative craft from a presenter who is happy to say the standard advice is wrong and then show why.

name: The Math Sorcerer
shortDescription: Ten thousand short videos on self-studying mathematics, heavy on which books to use and on the encouragement to keep going.

name: The Moth
shortDescription: A non-profit's archive of true personal stories told live without notes — the closest thing to a reference corpus for spoken storytelling.

name: The Plottery
shortDescription: A working fiction editor showing the fixes she actually makes to other people's manuscripts, in short lessons with a course bundle behind them.

name: Therapy in a Nutshell (Emma McAdam)
shortDescription: A licensed therapist teaching the specific skills used inside therapy, organised as numbered courses rather than as general reassurance.

name: The School of Life
shortDescription: Short, calm animated essays applying philosophy and psychotherapy to ordinary emotional life — insight-shaped rather than instruction-shaped.

name: The Speaker Lab
shortDescription: A podcast-led channel about the business of paid speaking — finding an audience, getting booked and pricing — rather than about delivery technique.

name: Think Fast Talk Smart (Matt Abrahams)
shortDescription: A Stanford business-school lecturer interviewing researchers and practitioners about specific communication problems, published as both podcast and clips.

name: This Guy Edits (Sven Pape)
shortDescription: A working feature-film editor who teaches mainly by recutting other people's footage on camera and explaining every decision.

name: Thomas Heaton
shortDescription: Landscape photography taught mostly through field vlogs — you watch him decide what to shoot and why, including when it does not work.

name: Toastmasters International
shortDescription: The official channel of the public-speaking membership organisation, mostly championship speeches and member stories rather than instruction.

name: Web Dev Simplified (Kyle Cook)
shortDescription: Broad, steady web-development teaching aimed at getting a beginner to full stack — mixed in with a lot of opinion pieces about the industry.

name: Wireless Philosophy
shortDescription: A finished, university-made animated curriculum on reasoning — fallacies, fundamentals and biases — in five-to-eight-minute pieces.
